solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Out of keeping, prom ripe for redevelopment (8)

indicatorNotes.for redevelopment: redeveloped letters are rebuilt in a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A seaside promenade that has gone shabby and is due to be rebuilt.
annotation.walkthrough: A prom here is a seafront promenade; the whole surface is about property, so the opening words look like a planner's verdict rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Something out of keeping is unsuitable for its setting, which is improper.

entries.clue: Boundless humour, one girl recollected, in famous old nightspot (6,5)

indicatorNotes.Boundless: without its bounds, the word loses its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.recollected: re-collected: gathered up again in a different order

blocks.note: HUMOUR without its outer letters H and R

annotation.surface: A night of unlimited laughs and a woman's memories of a celebrated club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as remembered, as if the girl is reminiscing; split as re-collected it tells you to gather the letters again. The Moulin Rouge is the Paris cabaret famous for the cancan.
annotation.definitionFit: The Moulin Rouge is a celebrated Parisian cabaret dating from 1889.

entries.clue: See 2 Down
Nice boarding house, I hesitate to say, for a senior citizen? (9)

blocks.note: a pension is a French boarding house, and Nice is in France
er is the sound of hesitation

annotation.surface: Someone hunting for a pleasant guesthouse suitable for an elderly relative.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective pleasant; it is the French city, which makes the boarding house French. The question mark admits that not every pensioner is elderly.
annotation.definitionFit: A pensioner draws a pension, usually because they are of retirement age.

entries.clue: Quote shortened during actual performance (7)

indicatorNotes.shortened: cut short, so the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.during: one piece sits within the time of the other, so it goes inside

blocks.note: actual = real; it wraps the other piece, RE…AL
CITE with its last letter cut

annotation.surface: A note that a quotation was trimmed while the show was actually on.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a critic's complaint, but 'actual' is only a synonym for REAL, split around the shortened quote.
annotation.definitionFit: A recital is a performance, typically of music or poetry by one performer.

entries.clue: Power feeding Tube centrally? The reverse in New York system (6)

indicatorNotes.centrally: take the central letters of the word
indicatorNotes.feeding: one thing going into another, so a container
indicatorNotes.The reverse: swap the roles just described: the tube goes into the power, not the power into the tube

blocks.note: sway = power, influence; it wraps the other piece, S…WAY
the middle two letters of tUBe

annotation.surface: Electricity supplying the London Tube, contrasted with the New York equivalent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' swaps the roles just described: the middle of the tube goes into the power, not the other way round. Tube is the London Underground; New York's equivalent is its subway.
annotation.definitionFit: The subway is New York City's underground railway system.

entries.clue: Auction, first of many in state capital (5)

indicatorNotes.first of: take the first letter of the word that follows

annotation.surface: An auction being the first of many held in a capital city.
annotation.walkthrough: Salem is the capital of the US state of Oregon.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Salem, Oregon, is one of the fifty US state capitals.

entries.clue: Exceptionally intelligent person was hard to indoctrinate (9)

blocks.note: a brain = a very clever person

annotation.surface: A remark that a brilliant person was difficult to convert to a creed.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'was hard to indoctrinate' as one phrase; it breaks after 'hard', and 'to' only links the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean forcing beliefs into someone's mind by pressure and repetition.

entries.clue: A pale worried deserter (8)

blocks.note: a pale is a fence stake, a post
ate = worried, as in 'what's eating you?'

annotation.surface: A deserter who looks pale and anxious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pale' and 'worried' look like two adjectives describing the deserter's face; both are hidden verbs or nouns. Pale as a noun is a stake, as in 'beyond the pale'.
annotation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons their faith or party, a deserter of a cause.

entries.clue: Colour of gold by Scottish brook (6)

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a burn is Scottish for a stream

annotation.surface: A golden glow beside a stream in the Scottish countryside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Colour of gold' looks like one phrase meaning golden; the definition is only 'Colour', and gold's chemical symbol sits beside the Scottish word for a stream.
annotation.definitionFit: Auburn is a reddish-brown colour, usually of hair.

entries.clue: A brandy and soda knocked back after five, after short visit (8)

indicatorNotes.short: cut short, so the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.knocked back: a drink knocked back goes down backwards: read it right to left
indicatorNotes.after: the piece is placed after the one named

blocks.note: CALL (a visit) with its last letter cut
V is the Roman numeral for five

annotation.surface: Someone downing a brandy and soda at five o'clock after a brief call.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'A' belongs to the definition, and 'knocked back' fits the drinking scene perfectly while telling you to reverse SODA.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Calvados is a Normandy spirit distilled from apple cider, one kind of brandy.

entries.clue: What one may be brought in a taverna with fashionable new tiles (4,4)

annotation.definition: What one may be brought in a taverna

indicatorNotes.new: the letters are made new, reshaped

annotation.surface: A Greek taverna done up with smart new tiling.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole descriptive phrase: a waiter in a Greek restaurant brings you the wine list. 'With' looks like a link but supplies the W.
annotation.definitionFit: A diner in a taverna may be handed the wine list to choose a drink.

entries.clue: Extremely small and quiet nursing home (6)

indicatorNotes.nursing: nursing holds something to itself, so this word goes around the next

blocks.note: mute = quiet; it wraps the other piece, M…UTE

annotation.surface: A tiny, peaceful nursing home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nursing home' is a fixed phrase in the surface; split, 'nursing' is the container instruction and 'home' gives IN.
annotation.definitionFit: Minute (pronounced my-NEWT) means extremely small.

entries.clue: Those seeking a relationship with belted earl, on the sly? (6,6)

indicatorNotes.belted: belted means struck hard, knocking the letters into a new order

annotation.surface: Secret romance with an aristocrat wearing a belt, perhaps an earl's ceremonial one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Belted earl' is a real phrase for an earl in formal dress, so 'belted' reads as a description rather than an instruction to beat the letters about.
annotation.definitionFit: Lonely hearts are single people looking for a partner, as in lonely-hearts columns.

entries.clue: Sluggish? It could be the garlic (9)

indicatorNotes.It could be: the answer could be made from these letters in another order

annotation.surface: Someone feeling sluggish wonders if the garlic they ate is to blame.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface blames a heavy meal; 'could be' is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish and lacking energy.

entries.clue: Casserole at bistro, ultimately a controversial issue (3,6)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: at the end: take the last letter

blocks.note: a hotpot is a meat and potato casserole

annotation.surface: A casserole ordered at a bistro turns out to be a divisive dish.
annotation.walkthrough: Lancashire hotpot is a traditional British casserole of meat topped with sliced potatoes.
annotation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an issue too controversial to handle comfortably.

entries.clue: Speak without restraint appealing to have conveniences installed (3,5)

indicatorNotes.to have: to have something is to hold it, here held within the other word
indicatorNotes.installed: plumbing that is installed is fitted into a building, so these letters are fitted inside

blocks.note: cute = appealing; it wraps the other piece, CUT…E
loos = toilets, conveniences in British English

annotation.surface: An attractive property with toilets fitted, praised with unrestrained enthusiasm.
annotation.walkthrough: Loo is British slang for toilet, and public conveniences are public toilets.
annotation.definitionFit: To cut loose is to let go of restraint, here in what one says.

entries.clue: Sweet bishop, say, having whisky (12)

annotation.surface: A kindly bishop, perhaps, enjoying a dram.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' attached to bishop; it is the verb UTTER. 'Sweet' reads as a description of the bishop rather than a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a sweet made from butter and brown sugar.

entries.clue: Constant battle over small wood (7)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, over means placed above, before

blocks.note: c is the constant for the speed of light
Ypres, Belgian town of several First World War battles
S = small, as in clothing sizes

annotation.surface: An unending fight over a little patch of woodland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Constant battle' reads as a phrase; 'Constant' alone gives C, the physics constant.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: cypress timber is one of many woods, prized for its durability.

entries.clue: Popular team, fundamentally (6)

annotation.surface: A team that is popular at its very core.
annotation.walkthrough: Inside as an adverb means at heart, deep down, which is fundamentally.
annotation.definitionFit: Inside, as in 'inside, he was kind', means at heart, fundamentally.

entries.clue: Impressionable one in factory (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the first piece goes inside the second

blocks.note: a plant is a factory; it wraps the other piece, PL…ANT

annotation.surface: A suggestible worker on a factory floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Impressionable one' reads as one phrase describing a person; 'one' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Pliant means easily influenced, impressionable.

entries.clue: Old character beginning to tune musical instrument (5)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a horn is a brass instrument

annotation.surface: An old eccentric starting to tune an instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old character' suggests an elderly eccentric; it is a letter of an old alphabet. Thorn, þ, was used in Old English for the th sound.
annotation.definitionFit: Thorn is the runic letter þ, an old character of the English alphabet.

entries.clue: Demanding deep thought, expert discovered (8)

blocks.note: a pro = an expert, a professional

annotation.surface: A deep problem that an expert finally cracked.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads the last two words as 'an expert was discovered'; they simply supply the two halves.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: profound ideas are deep ones that take hard thinking to grasp.

entries.clue: Complete circuit, or segment? (5)

blocks.note: a bit is a segment, a piece

annotation.surface: Asking whether to run a whole lap or just part of one.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets whole against part; the answer is built from 'or' and a part.
annotation.definitionFit: An orbit is one complete circuit of a body round another.

entries.clue: Perplex foremost of gardeners, appearing with passion flower (8)

indicatorNotes.foremost of: take the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: to fox is to baffle, perplex

annotation.surface: A leading gardener baffled by the appearance of a passion flower.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passion flower' is a real plant, so it looks like the definition; the definition is only 'flower', and 'passion' gives LOVE.
annotation.definitionFit: The foxglove is a tall flowering plant with tubular purple blooms.

entries.clue: Article, belt, I buckled, nevertheless (6)

indicatorNotes.buckled: bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An item of clothing, a belt, which I fastened anyway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buckled' fits a belt perfectly as fastened; here it means bent out of shape.
annotation.definitionFit: Albeit means although, even so: 'a small, albeit welcome, change'.

entries.clue: Member of the clergy made a confession, to some extent (6)

indicatorNotes.to some extent: only part of the following words is used

annotation.surface: A clergyman who partly owned up to something.
annotation.walkthrough: The confession suits a churchman, and the answer spans three words: maDE A CONfession.
annotation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister ranking below a priest.

entries.clue: A position on the cricket field, not long on (5,3)

annotation.definition: A position on the cricket field

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

annotation.surface: A fielder placed somewhere near but not at the position called long on.
annotation.walkthrough: Long on is itself a real cricket fielding position, so 'not long on' looks like a negation of it. In cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field.
annotation.definitionFit: Short leg is a close fielding position on the leg side near the batsman.
